title: Super Mario's bushes are secretly clouds
description: Super Mario Bros. squeezed into a tiny cartridge using clever tricks, like recolouring clouds into bushes.

scenes.say: The bushes in Super Mario Bros. are secretly clouds. Nintendo reused the same sprite with new colours to save space.
Same shape, different colours. On the NES, every byte mattered, so artists reused everything they possibly could.

scenes.caption: Built for the NES
scenes.say: Goombas are one image flipped back and forth. Getting hurt reuses the pipe sound. And with about twenty bytes left, Miyamoto added a crown beside your life counter at ten lives.
The whole game used roughly forty kilobytes for code and graphics combined. That is smaller than a single photo on your phone.
Some features were even inspired by glitches, like blocks that hold multiple coins. Limits made the game creative. Follow for more clever tricks.
